:::{#thm-wrong-code}
#### The cost of coding with the wrong distribution

Let $X$ take a finite number of values, with [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) $p$,
and let $q$ be such a function,
possibly different from $p$, with $q(x) > 0$ wherever $p(x) > 0$.
Suppose a code gives each value $x$ with $p(x) > 0$
the length $\ell(x) = \lceil -\log_2 q(x) \rceil$.
Then its [expected length](#def-expected-length) $L$ under $p$ satisfies

$$H_2(p, q) \le L < H_2(p, q) + 1,$$

where $H_2(p, q)$ is the
[cross-entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cross-entropy)
of $q$ relative to $p$, with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm).

:::

::: {.proof}

Every sum here runs over the values $x$ with $p(x) > 0$.
Rounding up adds less than one binary digit, so for each such $x$

$$-\log_2 q(x) \le \ell(x) < -\log_2 q(x) + 1.$$

Multiply each part by $p(x) > 0$ and sum.
Since $\sum_{x} p(x) = 1$,

$$
-\sum_{x} p(x) \log_2 q(x)
\le \sum_{x} p(x) \, \ell(x)
< -\sum_{x} p(x) \log_2 q(x) + 1.
$$

The middle sum is $L$ by @thm-expected-length-sum, and the outer sums are $H_2(p, q)$.

:::
